RQU2: Akal Purakh is One, and is found through the grace of the True Guru.
One Universal Creator God. By The Grace Of The True Guru:
There is but One God, By the True Guru's grace, is He attained.
9UY0: Raag Kalyan, Mahala 4: a Bani of eight-stanza hymns by Guru Ram Das ji.
Z1TV: Ram = pervading, all-pervading. Sun = hearing. Bheejai = is drenched (with the water of love).
Hearing (the Name of) the all-pervading Parmatma, (a person's) mind is drenched (with the water of love).
Hearing the Name of the Lord, the All-pervading Lord, my mind is drenched with joy.
O my Lord, hearing Your beauteous Name, my soul is mightily pleased.
O Ram! Uttering (ram) Your Name and hearing Your praise, my mind has become glad.
PLG6: Amrit = giving spiritual life. Sahje = in sahaj, remaining in spiritual poise. Peejai = can be drunk. ||1|| Rahau ||
This Name of Hari gives spiritual life and is delicious. This water of Hari's Name can be drunk (while remaining) in spiritual poise through the Guru's teaching. ||1|| Rahau ||
The Name of the Lord, Har, Har, is Ambrosial Nectar, the most Sweet and Sublime Essence; through the Guru's Teachings, drink it in with intuitive ease. ||1||Pause||
The Lord God's Name is an immortalising sweet ambrosia, which one in-drinks all-too spontaneously by the Guru's instructions. Pause.
O Hari Hari! The taste of the nectar of Your Name is very sweet; through the Guru's teaching let us drink it with ease. ||1|| Rahau ||
MTYJ: Kaast = wood. Mah = in. Baisantar = fire. Math = churning, rubbing. Sanjam = with method, with skill. Kaadh kadheejai = can be drawn out, can be produced.
Just as fire (lies hidden) in (every) piece of wood, (but) by effort with the right method it can be brought out,
The potential energy of fire is within the wood; it is released if you know how to rub it and generate friction.
As the fire is locked in the wood, but it is made manifest by the mortal who knows the way of rubbing the wood.
Just as fire is fully present in wood, and the one who draws it out draws it out by rubbing with discipline —
CR8U: Sabaaee = all (of creation). Tat = essence, secret, reality. ||1||
so Parmatma's Name is (such) that (its) light is (hidden) in all creation; this reality can be understood through the Guru's teaching. ||1||
In just the same way, the Lord's Name is the Light within all; the Essence is extracted by following the Guru's Teachings. ||1||
So is the light of the Lord's Name within all, but its quintessence if found through the Guru's teachings.
O Named One, Ram! So Your light has come into all; through the Guru's teaching it is drawn out — meaning directly realised. ||1||
96Y2: Nave = all nine. Dasve = through the tenth (door). Chueejai = trickles.

(The human body) has nine doors (through which a person stays linked with the outside world, but) all nine of these doors stay dry (of the taste of the Name). The taste of Hari's Name, which gives spiritual life, trickles (within a person) only through the tenth door (the mind, as essence trickles through a still's tube).
There are nine doors, but the taste of these nine doors is bland and insipid. The Essence of Ambrosial Nectar trickles down through the Tenth Door.
The body has nine doors but insipid is the relish of all the nine doors. It is in the tenth one, that the immortalising Nectar trickles.
The nine openings that are visible — these nine doors of the body — are tasteless, and for the yogi the nectar taste (chueejai) trickles from the tenth door.
VBQP: Piare = O Beloved! Sabdee = through the Word. Peejai = can be drunk. ||2||
O Beloved Prabhu! Always show mercy (on Your beings); (if You show mercy, then) through the blessing of the Guru's Word this taste of Hari's Name can be drunk. ||2||
Please take pity on me - be kind and compassionate, O my Beloved, that I may drink in the Sublime Essence of the Lord, through the Word of the Guru's Shabad. ||2||
Show You Your mercy, compassion and Kindness to me, O my Love, that I may in-drink the Lord's Name elixir through the Guru's word.
O Hari, form of grace, mine of grace, Beloved! Cast a glance of grace on us, that we may meet the Guru, and through the Guru's teaching, O Hari, drink in Your taste. ||2||
JH5P: Kaia = body. Neeko = good, beautiful. Vich = within (the body). Keejai = should be done.
The human body is (as it were a) city; in this (body-city) one should keep trading to (buy) the taste of Hari's Name.
The body-village is the most sublime and exalted village, in which the merchandise of the Lord's Sublime Essence is traded.
The body abode is the beauteous Township in which the business of the God's Nectar is transacted.
Of all cities, the city that is the body is most beautiful. Within it, O Hari, let us trade in the taste of the Name.
5005: Amol = which cannot be bought at any price. Leejai = can be gained. ||3||
(This taste of Hari's Name is, as it were,) priceless jewels and rubies; (this taste of Hari's Name) can be gained only by taking the Guru's shelter. ||3||
The most precious and priceless gems and jewels are obtained by serving the True Guru. ||3||
Precious, the most precious jewels and emeralds are attained through the True Guru's service.
The most priceless jewels and rubies, which are detachment and love, are gained by serving the True Guru. ||3||
S9DZ: Agam = unreachable. Bhar = filled (with priceless jewels and rubies). Bhar saagar bhagat = devotion to Prabhu, the ocean filled (with priceless rubies and jewels). Kareejai = can be done.
The Guru is (the form of) the unreachable Parmatma. Devotion to the ocean (Prabhu), filled (with priceless jewels and rubies), can be done (only by taking the Guru's shelter).
The True Guru is Inaccessible; Inaccessible is our Lord and Master. He is the overflowing Ocean of bliss - worship Him with loving devotion.
Unfathomable and Inscrutable is the Lord, who is the brimful ocean of bliss. Through the true Guru, embrace you, His loving adoration.
O most unreachable Thakur! Through the True Guru, in this world-ocean filled with the water of the Name, let us do Your devotion.
QHC5: Deen = humble. Saaring = rain-birds (papeeha). Mukh = in (my) mouth. Deejai = give. ||4||

O Prabhu! We beings are humble rain-birds (at Your door). Show mercy, show mercy: (as the rain-bird thirsts for) a single drop (of rain, so I thirst for the water of Your Name) — give (Your) Name (-water) into (my) mouth. ||4||
Please take pity on me, and be Merciful to this meek song-bird; please pour a drop of Your Name into my mouth. ||4||
O Lord, show You mercy and compassion to me, the meek sparrow hawk and pour into my mouth a drop of Your Name.
O mine of grace! Casting a glance of grace on me, a humble rain-bird, give into my mouth a single drop of svaati rain — the Name. ||4||
M8X4: Laalan = the beautiful ruby, the beautiful Name of Hari. Rangan = beautiful dye. Gur = O Guru! Deejai = give.
The beautiful Hari (-Name) is a most beautiful dye. O Guru! Give (me this dye of Hari's Name) to dye (my) mind.
O Beloved Lord, please color my mind with the Deep Crimson Color of Your Love; I have surrendered my mind to the Guru.
To gladden, gladden my mind, O my Guru, bless you me with the loving adoration on the loved, loved Beloved.
O (laal) Beloved! Give me, through the Guru, Your crimson dye — that is, devotion — to dye crimson the cloth of the mind.
X487: Rang = in the colour. Raate = are dyed. Ras rasik = lovers of the taste of the Name. Gatak = gulp by gulp, with relish. Peejai = should be drunk. ||5||

(Those who receive this dye of the Name) stay dyed for ever in the colour of Parmatma's (Name); (they become) lovers of the taste (of the Name). (This taste of the Name) should be drunk always, gulp by gulp. ||5||
Those who are imbued with the Love of the Lord, Raam, Raam, Raam, continually drink in this essence in big gulps, savoring its sweet taste. ||5||
O my Lord, God, the All-pervading God, they, who are imbued with Your love, ever tastefully in-drink in big draughts, Your Name-Nectar.
O Ram! Those who in mind and speech are dyed in Your (rang) love become (rasik) lovers and drink the taste of Your Name in gulps — that is, steadily — every day. ||5||
DRSB: Basudha = the earth. Sapat = seven. Deep = (dveep) islands, continents. Saagar = (the seven) seas. Kanchan = gold.
(All) the earth there is, with its seven continents and seven seas — (if it were) dug up and (all the) gold taken out (of it) and set (before them),
If all the gold of the seven continents and the oceans was taken out and placed before them,
If the gold of the seven continents and oceans of the earth be taken out and placed before them.
If the gold of the earth's seven continents were taken out, and the jewels of the seven seas taken out, and all set in one place —
A2WX: Inahu = these precious things. Baachhahi = want, long for. Maagahi = ask for. Deejai = give. ||6||

(even then) the devotees of my Master-Prabhu do not want these (precious things, gold and the rest); they always ask for Parmatma (His Name alone). O Guru! Grant (me too) only the taste of Parmatma's Name. ||6||
the humble servants of my Lord and Master would not even want it. They beg for the Lord to bless them with the Lord's Sublime Essence. ||6||
My Lord's slave desire it not. They beg their Lord. God for the grant of His Name elixir.
O my Thakur! Your servants do not want these. O Hari! They ask that You give them the taste of Hari's Name. ||6||
Y56W: Saakat = people cut off from Parmatma. Sad = always. Bhookhe = caught in greed for Maya. Bhookhan bhookh kareejai = keep crying out only their hunger (for Maya).
People cut off from Parmatma stay forever caught in greed for Maya; (within them) the cry of hunger — hunger (for Maya) — goes on for ever.
The faithless cynics and mortal beings remain hungry forever; they continually cry out in hunger.
Ever hungry remain the apostate persons and mortals. Hunger, hunger they ever cry out.
The self-willed mortals stay forever hungry for things, and every day cry (bhookhan bhookh) "hunger, only hunger".
G82L: Dhaavat = wandering. Dhai = having wandered. Dhaavahi = wander. Dhaavat dhai dhaavahi = wandering, having wandered, they wander; they wander about for ever. Lakh kosan kau = to hundreds of thousands of kos. Bith deejai = a gap is made. ||7||
Because of the pull of Maya, they wander about for ever. (For the sake of gathering Maya, between their mind and Parmatma) a gap of hundreds of thousands of kos is made. ||7||
They hurry and run, and wander all around, caught in the love of Maya; they cover hundreds of thousands of miles in their wanderings. ||7||
They run, roam under about through the love of riches and cover a distance of lacs of miles.

Through love of Maya, running after (dhaavat) things that (dhai) are bound to perish, they put a gap of hundreds of thousands of kos — that is, very many kos — behind them; meaning they leave their own home and go off to foreign lands. ||7||
RE6K: Har jan = Parmatma's devotees. Kia upma = what praise? Deejai = could be given.
Through the blessing of always chanting Hari's Name, Parmatma's devotees become of lofty life; no praise of them can be (fully) made.
The humble servants of the Lord, Har, Har, Har, Har, Har, are sublime and exalted. What praise can we bestow upon them?
Sublime are you Lord God, Master's, yea, Lord God's saints. What praise can one attribute to them?
O Hari! Your saints, chanting Your Name "Hari Hari", have become green (flourishing) in mind and body. So they are excellent; to what could they be compared?

MBYF: Tul = equal. Aur upma = any other praise. Kripa kareejai = show grace. ||8||1||
There is no other thing equal to Parmatma's Name. O Prabhu! Show mercy on (Your) servant Nanak (and grant Your Name). ||8||1||
Nothing else can equal the Glory of the Lord's Name; please bless servant Nanak with Your Grace. ||8||1||
O Lord, take you pity on slave Nanak and bless him with Your Name, the like of which there is no other magnificence.
O Ram! Those who chant You have no other likeness equal to them — meaning they alone are like themselves. Sri Guru ji says: in grace, give me the company of those servants. ||8||1||
RC36: Ram = O Ram! O Hari! Paaras = the stone whose touch is believed to turn iron into gold. Paras = touch (with the Guru). Kareejai = make it happen.
O Hari! The Guru is (the true) philosopher's stone; bring about (my) touch (with the Guru) — (unite me with the Guru).
O Lord, please bless me with the Touch of the Guru, the Philosopher's Stone.
My Lord, bless You me with the touch of the Guru, the philosopher's stone.
O Ram! Bring about our touch — that is, union — with the Guru, the form of the philosopher's stone.
LMCV: Ham = we beings. Nirgunee = without virtue. Manoor = burnt iron, slag. At pheeke = of very dry, tasteless life. Mil satgur = meeting the Guru. Keejai = show (this mercy). ||1|| Rahau ||
We beings are without virtue; we are burnt iron; we are of very dry life. Show (this mercy), that meeting the Guru (we may become) the philosopher's stone. ||1|| Rahau ||
I was unworthy, utterly useless, rusty slag; meeting with the True Guru, I was transformed by the Philosopher's Stone. ||1||Pause||
I was the meritless and exceedingly worthless rusted iron. Meeting with the True Guru, I am transmuted into an invaluable personality.
We are without virtues, like slag — that is, heavy with sins — and utterly tasteless. Unite us with the True Guru and make us like the philosopher's stone. ||1|| Rahau ||
GYGM: Sabh = all people. Baanchhahi = ask for. Nit = always. Kareejai = is being done.
All people keep asking for heaven, liberation, Baikunth; (for heaven, liberation, Baikunth alone) hope is always being placed.
Everyone longs for paradise, liberation and heaven; all place their hopes in them.
Everyone longs for paradise emancipation and elysium and ever rests all his hopes on them.
Everyone wants heaven and liberation, and Baikunth too, and full of hope they hope for it every day.
QL2S: Mil = meeting (Hari). Darsan tripat = with the fulfilment of Hari's sight. Dheejai = comes to patience, becomes calm. ||1||
But the devotees who love Parmatma's sight do not ask for liberation. Meeting (Parmatma), (their) mind stays calm in the fulfilment of (Parmatma's) sight. ||1||
The humble long for the Blessed Vision of His Darshan; they do not ask for liberation. Their minds are satisfied and comforted by His Darshan. ||1||
The Persons desirous of the God's vision ask not for emancipation. Obtaining His vision, their soul is satiated and comforted.
O Hari! The people who long for Your sight do not even want liberation; meeting You and seeing You, their mind is fulfilled and holds patience. ||1||
BHH7: Sabal = mighty. Kaalakh daag = the stain of the soot of vices.
(In the world) attachment to Maya is very mighty; attachment (to Maya) puts stains of the soot (of vices on beings' minds).
Emotional attachment to Maya is very powerful; this attachment is a black stain which sticks.
Highly powerful is the attachment of mammon and this attachment brands one with the black spot.
For those in whom attachment to Maya is (sabal hai bhaaree) extremely strong, through attachment the stain of the soot of sins falls on their face.
VUZC: Alipat = unstained, detached. Mukte = saved from vices. Pank = wing, feather. ||2||
But Parmatma's devotees stay unstained (by attachment to Maya); they stay saved from vices, just as a water-bird's wing does not get wet (in water). ||2||
The humble servants of my Lord and Master are unattached and liberated. They are like ducks, whose feathers do not get wet. ||2||
Detached and emancipated are the saints of my Lord, like the duck, whose wings are wetted not.
O my Thakur! Your devotees, being unattached to that Maya, are (mukte) free. Just as the water-bird does not get its (pank) feathers wet in water or mud, so the saints stay unstained in Maya. ||2||
9A9P: Vaas = fragrance. Bhuiangam = snakes. Verree = surrounded. Kiv = how. Mileeai = can be met. Leejai = can be taken.

The fragrance of sandalwood stays surrounded by snakes. How can (the sandalwood) be reached? How can the sandalwood be gained? (A person's soul stays surrounded by vices; the fragrance of union with Prabhu does not reach them.)
The fragrant sandalwood tree is encircled by snakes; how can anyone get to the sandalwood?
The fragrant sandal tree is girdled by the snakes; how can one reach and get to the sandal tree?
The fragrance of the sandalwood that is the bliss of the self is (verree) covered by the snakes of lust and the rest. So how may we meet it, and take that sandalwood?
03TK: Kharrag = sword. Gur giaan = the knowledge given by the Guru. Giaan = understanding of spiritual life. Karaara = strong. Bikh = poison. Chhed = cutting. Peejai = can be drunk. ||3||

The knowledge (the understanding of spiritual life) given by the Guru is a sharp sword; drawing (this sword) and cutting and cutting away (at the roots) the poison (of attachment to Maya, which kills spiritual life), the taste of the Name can be drunk. ||3||
Drawing out the Mighty Sword of the Guru's Spiritual Wisdom, I slaughter and kill the poisonous snakes, and drink in the Sweet Nectar. ||3||
Drawing out the powerful sword of the Guru's gnosis and killing and destroying there with the poisonous snakes, in-drinks I the Name-Nectar.

When the Guru drew out for us the (karaara) strong (kharrag) sword of spiritual knowledge, with it we cut and cut the snakes of lust and the rest, and drink the taste of the self. ||3|| ☬ Now he speaks of the greatness of the Name:
6ZS2: Aan = bringing. Aan aan = bringing and bringing. Samdha = a pile of wood. Baisantar = fire. Bhasam = ash. Kareejai = can be made.
If wood is brought and brought and a great pile of wood gathered, fire (a single spark) can turn (it) to ash in a moment.
You may gather wood and stack it in a pile, but in an instant, fire reduces it to ashes.
Bringing and gathering wood, one stacks it in t heap, but, in a moment, the fire reduces it to ashes.
Just as, bringing and bringing (samdha) firewood, a great heap is gathered, and fire burns that heap to ash in a single moment —
XLPE: Ugr = terrible, huge. Saakat = people cut off from Parmatma. Mil saadhoo = meeting the Guru. Lookee = a burning brand. Deejai = can be applied. ||4||
People cut off from Parmatma commit very great and terrible sins; (to burn those sins,) meeting the Guru, the burning brand (of the fire of Hari's Name) can be applied. ||4||
The faithless cynic gathers the most horrendous sins, but meeting with the Holy Saint, they are placed in the fire. ||4||
Similarly, the apostate persons has gathered very heinous sins, but, meeting with the Saint Guru, he applies fire to them.
in the same way, the terrible sins the saakat has committed are destroyed in a moment by meeting the holy ones and applying the (lookee) burning brand of uttering the Name. ||4||
85TC: Saadhoo = people who keep their mind under control. Neeke = good, fine, virtuous. Jin antar = within whom.
The people in whose heart Parmatma's Name stays settled — they are the holy ones; they are the good people.
The Holy, Saintly devotees are sublime and exalted. They enshrine the Naam, the Name of the Lord, deep within.
Sublime are the saints, devotees and saintly persons, who enshrine the Lord's Name within their mind.
Those who have held the Name in their hearts — those holy ones who practise discipline are most excellent.
KGM2: Parsan = through the touch (of Hari's Name). Paras = the philosopher's stone. Jan = as if. Dikheejai = has become visible (to them). ||5||
Through the touch (of Parmatma's Name, those people) have become holy; (to them,) as it were, Hari Bhagvan has become visible (everywhere). ||5||
By the touch of the Holy and the humble servants of the Lord, the Lord God is seen. ||5||
Seeing the saints, I have becomes happy, It is through the saints that the Lord God is seen.
Even those who were (niparas) not fit to be touched — that is, of low caste — by (paras) meeting the holy ones and seeing You, O Hari Bhagvan, have become pure, like the Bhil woman and others. ||5||
QTSU: Saakat soot = the thread of life of one cut off from Parmatma. Gurjhee = with tangles. Kiu kar = how? Taan = the warp of life. Taneejai = can be woven.
The thread of life of a person cut off from Parmatma stays full of countless tangles (of vices).
The thread of the faithless cynic is totally knotted and tangled; how can anything be woven with it?
The thread of an apostate is knotted with good many entanglements. How can the warp be weaved out of it?
The thread that is the inner mind of the self-willed is full of (gurjhee) very hard knots of many desires, or of crookedness; so how can the warp of purity be woven?
CE88: Tant = strand. Soot = thread. Nikasai = comes out. Sang = company. ||6||

(With a thread of life full of tangles of vices, the) warp (of pure life) cannot be woven at all, (for from those tangles not one straight) strand comes out, not one thread comes out. (So, O brother!) The company of a person cut off from Parmatma should not be kept. ||6||
This thread cannot be woven into yarn; do not associate with those faithless cynics. ||6||
His (cotton of) deeds yield no yarn and thread of virtue. So, associate you not with the mammon-worshipper.

No straight thread of the strand of thought comes out — that is, only bad thread comes out; so the company of the self-willed is not kept — meaning we do not keep the company of the self-willed. ||6||
WYFW: Satgur saadh sangat = the Guru's holy company. Neekee = good. Mil = meeting. Raveejai = can be remembered.
The Guru's holy company is good (company); joining the holy company, Parmatma's Name can be chanted.
The True Guru and the Saadh Sangat, the Company of the Holy, are exalted and sublime. Joining the Congregation, meditate on the Lord.
Sublime is the True Guru and the saints society, meeting and associating with whom, the Lord is meditated upon.
The True Guru is (saadh) most excellent, and His company too is most excellent; joining that company, O Ram, we (raveejai) chant You.
NV3R: Antar = within (a person). Maanak = pearls. Te = from, through. Leejai = can be taken. ||7||
Within (a person, hidden, lies Hari's Name, as it were) jewels, gems and pearls; (this Name of Hari, staying in the holy company,) can be taken through the Guru's grace. ||7||
The gems, jewels and precious stones are deep within; by Guru's Grace, they are found. ||7||
Within the mind are gems, jewels and emeralds, it is through the Guru's grace that one attain to them.

Within the mind itself are jewels, gems, rubies and such things — that is, detachment, spiritual knowledge, reflection and the rest are within the inner mind itself — but they are taken through the Guru's grace. ||7||
6H06: Thakur = Master-Prabhu. Milah = we can meet. Mileejai = can be met.
My Master, my Lord, is very great; how can we beings meet (Him by our own effort)? (In this way He) cannot be met.
My Lord and Master is Glorious and Great. How can I be united in His Union?
Great and magnificent is my Lord Master. How can I unite in His union?
O Swami! You are my Thakur, greater than the greatest. How can we meet You? You unite us with Yourself.
A9NC: Mel = joining (to His Word). Kau = to. Pooran = the state of completeness. Deejai = give. ||8||2||

O Nanak! The perfect Guru (alone), joining (a person to His Word), unites (them with Parmatma). (So one should keep praying at the door of the Guru-Parmeshar: O Prabhu!) Grant (Your) servant the state of completeness. ||8||2||
O Nanak, the Perfect Guru unites His humble servant in His Union, and blesses him with perfection. ||8||2||
Nanak, the perfect Guru, unites man in the Lord's union and blesses him with the state of perfect bliss.

Sri Guru ji says: the perfect True Guru, through union with the true company, unites (the being) in Your union; so, uniting me, Your servant, with the Guru, give me the complete state. The meaning of this last hymn can also be taken as teaching. ||8||2||
Z52F: Ram = all-pervading. Ramo Ram = Ram alone. Raveejai = should be remembered.
(The Name of) the all-pervading Ram should always be remembered.
Chant the Name of the Lord, the Lord, the All-pervading Lord.
O my beauteous all pervading God, I utter the Lord's Name alone.
O Ram! Let us, in mind and speech, dwell in Your (ram) beautiful Name, Ram.
QPJZ: Neeke = good, of pure life. Mil = meeting. Har rang = the bliss (of union) with Hari. ||1|| Rahau ||
(Only through the blessing of remembrance do people) become holy Gurmukhs of lofty life. Meeting the holy ones, one should enjoy the bliss of union with Parmatma. ||1|| Rahau ||
The Holy, the humble and Holy, are noble and sublime. Meeting with the Holy, I joyfully love the Lord. ||1||Pause||
Sublime are the saints, devotees and the saintly persons. Meeting with the saints, I am attuned to my Lord. Pause.
The holy ones who are (saadh) blessed and most excellent — joining those holy ones, O Hari, let us love You. ||1|| Rahau ||
CAYW: Sabh jag = the whole world. Jeta = as much as there is. Dolat dol kareejai = keeps wavering at every moment.
O Hari! As much of the world as there is — the mind of (all) its beings keeps wavering at every moment (under the influence of Maya).
The minds of all the beings and creatures of the world waver unsteadily.
The world and all the creatures, that are there, their minds, ever wabble and wobble.
However much of the world there is, small and great beings — the mind of all is wavering greatly.
6SB8: Kar = showing. Saadh = the Guru. Thamman kau = to support. Deejai = give. ||1||
O Prabhu! Show mercy, show mercy: unite (beings) with the Guru (the Guru is the pillar for the world); give (this) pillar to support the world. ||1||
Please take pity on them, be merciful to them, and unite them with the Holy; establish this support to support the world. ||1||
O Lord, mercifully and compassionately, unite You them with the saints and thus support the world, by giving them the support.
O mine of grace! In grace, unite me with the holy one, and give the (thamm) support of the Guru's Word to stop (jag) birth and death. ||1||
8XCA: Basudha = the earth. Talai talai = always under the feet. Ruleejai = one should roll in, should stay lying.
The earth always stays under the feet (of beings), (and in the end) comes on top of all. Meeting the Guru, one should stay settled under the feet (of all).
The earth is beneath us, and yet its dust falls down on all; let yourself be covered by the dust of the feet of the Holy.
The dust is beneath the feet of all and, from beneath, it falls over all. Roll you, therefore, in the dust of the saints feet.
O Bhagvan! Just as the earth, by staying under everyone's soles, becomes dust and comes on top of all, so let us roll at the feet of the holy — meaning, let us become very humble.
VT65: Ootam = of lofty life. Sabh sisat = all creation. Deejai = can be given. ||2||
(If you walk this road of life,) you will become of the very loftiest life; (through the blessing of humility) the whole earth can be placed under (your) feet. ||2||
You shall be utterly exalted, the most noble and sublime of all; the whole world will place itself at your feet. ||2||
Thiswise, you shall become the most sublime, yea, the most sublime and the whole world shall place its head below your feet.
Then one becomes the most excellent of the excellent, and all creation bows its head beneath that person's feet. ||2||
HTUR: Siv jot = Parmatma's light. Neekee = good. Gurmukh = staying facing the Guru. Aan paanee = bringing water. Sakat = Maya.
Taking the Guru's shelter, the good and beautiful light of Parmatma (is lit within a person; then) Maya (too) brings and fills water (for them) (Maya becomes their servant).
The Gurmukhs are blessed with the Divine Light of the Lord; Maya comes to serve them.
The Guru-ward is blessed with the Lord's blessed and sublime light and the mammon comes and pays obeisance to him.
O (Siv) form of well-being! The Gurmukhs have attained Your good, fine light, and Maya comes and fills their water.
BAD2: Main dant = teeth of wax, gentleness of heart. Saar = iron. Saar chab chab = bringing the mighty vices under control. Peejai = can be drunk. ||3||
Through the Guru's words (such) gentleness arises in their heart that, bringing the mighty vices under control, Parmatma's taste of the Name can be drunk. ||3||
Through the Word of the Guru's Teachings, they bite with teeth of wax and chew iron, drinking in the Sublime Essence of the Lord. ||3||
By the Guru's word, he cuts the teeth of wax (of compassion), bites and chews the hard iron(sin)and thiswise in-drinks the God's elixir.

Teeth of (main) wax — that is, gentle detachment and discernment — have come forth through the Guru's words, and chewing and chewing the world, which is (saar) iron — that is, negating it — O Hari, they drink the taste of Your Name. ||3||
KCGB: Anugrah = grace, gift. Mileejai = one should meet.
One should meet the holy Guru, the Being; the Guru shows the mercy of giving the gift of Parmatma's Name.
The Lord has shown great mercy, and bestowed His Name; I have met with the Holy Guru, the Primal Being.
The Lord God has shown great mercy to me and I have met with the Guru, the saintly person.
O Named One, Ram! You have shown me very great (anugrah) grace, because You have united me with the Guru, the most excellent Being.
5JM5: Bistheeran keeai = spread out. Sagal bhavan = in all realms, in the whole world. Jas = praise. Deejai = is shared out. ||4||
The Guru spreads Parmatma's Name, Parmatma's virtues, (through the whole world); (through the Guru) Parmatma's praise is shared out in all realms. ||4||
The Glorious Praises of the Lord's Name have spread out everywhere; the Lord bestows fame all over the world. ||4||
The praises of the Lord's Name, I have spread all around and the Lord has blessed me with glory all the world over.
Through His teaching, O Ram, they are spreading Your Name and virtues. O Hari! In all the realms You have given me praise. ||4||
C1TA: Saadh man = in the minds of the saints. Reh na sakeejai = cannot remain.
In the minds of the saints the Beloved Prabhu (always) dwells; without seeing (Prabhu) they cannot remain.
The Beloved Lord is within the minds of the Holy, the Holy Saadhus; without seeing Him, they cannot survive.
Within the mind of every saint, the devotee and the saintly person, is my Beloved Lord and he can lives not without seeing Him.
They alone are the most excellent holy ones who, (saadh) controlling the mind, O Beloved, cannot live without You. ☬ Why can they not live? He says:
J29Q: Jal meen = the fish of the water. Jalan jal preet = love of water at every moment. Phoot = bursting, writhing. ||5||
Just as the fish of the water loves only water at every moment, and without water, in an instant, writhes and dies. ||5||
The fish in the water loves only the water. Without water, it bursts and dies in an instant. ||5||
As the water fish bears love to water alone and without water, it bursts to death in a moment, so is my affection for the Saint-Guru.
Just as the fish lives in water and its love is for water and water alone, and without that water it bursts and dies in an instant — meaning it dies in suffering. ||5||

4Z7K: Abhaag = bad fortune. Saadhoo dhoor = the dust of the saints' feet.
The people whose fortune is very bad are not blessed with the dust of the saints' feet.
Those who have terrible luck and bad fortune do not drink in the water which washes the dust of the feet of the Holy.
Those, who have exceedingly bad luck, do not eat the dust of the feet of the saints.
The unfortunate ones whose fortune is most unlucky have not washed the dust of Your saints' feet and drunk that water.
JEWA: Nahee boojhahi = do not become calm. Dand = punishment. Deejai = is given. ||6||
Within them the fire of craving keeps burning; burning at every moment, (within them) no coolness comes. (This is the) punishment of Dharamraj (they receive). ||6||
The burning fire of their desires is not extinguished; they are beaten and punished by the Righteous Judge of Dharma. ||6||
The burning fire of their cravings is stilled not and they suffer punishment at the hands of the Righteous Judge.
Their mind burns with craving, and that burning is not put out; in the next world they receive the punishment of Dharamrai. ||6|| ☬ Now he speaks of the glory of the Name:
XAXT: Sabh = all. Hivai = in the snow. Gaal = wasting away. Tan chheejai = (if) the body is destroyed.
If bathing at all the pilgrimage places, countless fasts, yagyas and other (such) acts of merit and charity are done, (and) the body is wasted away and destroyed in the snow (in mountain caves),
You may visit all the sacred shrines, observe fasts and sacred feasts, give generously in charity and waste away the body, melting it in the snow.
Man may visit all the holies, observe fasting, perform sacred feasts, give generously in charity and destroy his body by wasting and dissipating it in snow.
All pilgrimages, fasts and yagyas, and many acts of merit too, were done, and the body was wasted away in the Himalaya mountains and destroyed —
17HV: Atula = that cannot be weighed. Ko = any (effort). Pujai na = does not reach, cannot equal. Tuleejai = if it is weighed. ||7||
(even then, of all these practices) no practice can equal Parmatma's Name. Parmatma's Name is such that no weight can weigh it; it is found by walking on the Guru's teaching. ||7||
The weight of the Lord's Name is unweighable, according to the Guru's Teachings; nothing can equal its weight. ||7||
But, heavier is the weight of the merit of contemplating the Lord's Name, through the Guru's instructions, In weight nothings can equal the weight of the Name's meditation.

Chanting Ram's Name through the Guru's teaching — its weight is beyond weighing; no practice that has been weighed reaches that weight, even if one weighs it on the scales of the intellect; meaning the practices above are not equal to Ram's Name. ||7||
VUKC: Braham = O Prabhu! Tav = Your. Pareejai = one should stay lying.
O servant Nanak! (Pray:) O Prabhu! You (Yourself alone) know Your virtues; (show mercy, that we beings) may stay in (Your) shelter.
O God, You alone know Your Glorious Virtues. Servant Nanak seeks Your Sanctuary.
Yours virtues, O Lord God, You alone know. Slave Nanak has sought Your refuge.
O Braham! Your virtues, which are expounded by the (braham) Veda, You alone know. Sri Guru ji says: we have come to Your shelter.
MJBP: Jalnidh = treasure of water, ocean. Kar = showing. Sang = with (You). ||8||3||
You are (our) ocean; we beings are Your fish. Showing mercy, keep (us) with (You). ||8||3||
You are the Ocean of water, and I am Your fish. Please be kind, and keep me always with You. ||8||3||
You are the ocean of water and I am a fish of Yours Mercifully Keep You me ever with You.
O Bhagvan! You are like the ocean and we are Your fish; O Maharaj! Casting a glance of grace, keep me with You. ||8||3||
P586: Ram = all-pervading. Pooj = devotion. Kareejai = should be done.
Devotion to the all-pervading Parmatma should always be done.
I worship and adore the Lord, the All-pervading Lord.
I worship only the All-pervading Lord's God.
O (Ram) form who pervades all, beautiful (ram) Ram! We do Your worship.
QC0H: Arap = offering. Dharau = I place. Sabh = everything. Giaan = understanding of spiritual life. Drirreejai = may become firm in the heart. ||1|| Rahau ||

If anyone, through the Guru's teaching, makes the joy of Parmatma's Name and the understanding of spiritual life firm in my heart, I would place my mind, my body, everything as an offering before them. ||1|| Rahau ||
I surrender my mind and body, and place everything before Him; following the Guru's Teachings, spiritual wisdom is implanted within me. ||1||Pause||
Surrendering my soul and body, I place them all before Him and, through the Guru's teaching, implant I the ambrosial Divine knowledge within me. Pause.
I have offered my mind, body and everything before You; through the Guru's teaching make the taste of spiritual knowledge firm in me. ||1|| Rahau ||
97Z1: Braham naam = Parmatma's Name. Braham gun = Parmatma's praise. Saakh tarovar = the branches of a tree. Chun chun = picking and picking (these very flowers). Pooj kareejai = worship should be done.
Parmatma's Name and Parmatma's virtues are the branches of the tree (from which, picking and picking the flowers of the Name and of praise), Parmatma-Dev should be worshipped.
God's Name is the tree, and His Glorious Virtues are the branches. Picking and gathering up the fruit, I worship Him.
The Lord's Name is the tree and virtues its branches. Picking and gathering up the virtues, I ever worship them.
The (braham) Veda is the tree; Your Names are its branches and Your virtues its flowers. Picking and picking these flowers, let us worship You every day — meaning, let us sing Your praises.
SJR5: Aatam deu = Parmatma alone is the deity. Ras laagai = attached to the taste (of Parmatma's Name). ||1||
Parmatma alone is the deity (worthy of worship); attached to the taste (of Parmatma's Name), one should worship Parmatma alone. ||1||
The soul is divine; divine is the soul. Worship Him with love. ||1||
The Luminous Lord is the llluminator of the human soul. With utter love, adore you Him.
O Aatam Deu! You are the form of light and the self of all; the devotees who are attached to Your (ras) love do Your worship. ||1||
UH3S: Bibek budh = the intellect that can test good and bad deeds. Bichar bichar = reflecting and reflecting (through this intellect). Peejai = should be drunk.

(Above all other cleverness) in the world, the intellect that can test good and bad deeds is the purest. (With its help, settling Parmatma's virtues in the mind again and again,) one should drink the taste (of the Name, which gives spiritual life).
One of keen intellect and precise understanding is immaculate in all this world. In thoughtful consideration, he drinks in the sublime essence.
Immaculate in the entire world is the man of discerning intellect. Reflecting over and contemplating the Lord, he in-drinks the nectar.
A person of discerning intellect is pure in all the world, and, reflecting and reflecting, drinks the taste of the Name.
8N47: Parsad = by the grace. Padaarath = the Name of Hari. Kau = to. Deejai = should be given. ||2||
This treasure of the Name is found (only) by the Guru's grace; one should hand this mind of one's own over to the Guru. ||2||
By Guru's Grace, the treasure is found; dedicate this mind to the True Guru. ||2||
Dedicating this soul to the True Guru and by the Guru's grace, I have attained to the Name wealth.
Through the Guru's pleasure I have found the treasure of Your Name; that is why I have given this mind to the True Guru. ||2||
62XL: At neeko = very beautiful. Heero = the diamond of Hari's Name. Heerai = with (this) diamond. Heer = the diamond of the mind. Bidheejai = should be pierced, should be strung.
The diamond of Parmatma's Name is very precious and very beautiful; with this diamond of the Name, one should keep (one's mind-) diamond always strung.
Priceless and utterly sublime is the Diamond of the Lord. This Diamond pierces the diamond of the mind.
Invaluable and supremely sublime is the Name diamond of the Lord. With this diamond the mind's diamond is pierced through.
The Guru's teaching, priceless like a most excellent diamond — with that diamond the diamond of the mind has been pierced.
3MNK: Saal = the best, most excellent. Sabdee = through the Word. Jit = through the blessing of which (Word). Heera = the diamond of the Name. ||3||
Through the Guru's Word this mind can become an excellent pearl, because through the blessing of the Word one comes to understand the worth of the diamond of the Name. ||3||
The mind becomes the jeweller, through the Word of the Guru's Shabad; it appraises the Diamond of the Lord. ||3||
Through the Guru's word, the mind becomes the jeweller, which then, assays God, the diamond.
The mind of a person of the Guru's Word is a (saal) most excellent pearl — the mind is pure; and with that mind, O Braham, form of the diamond, You are tested and recognised. ||3||
KAPM: Sang = with. Lag = clinging. Peep = the pipal tree. Palaas = the palaas (chhichhra) tree.
Staying in the company of the saints and clinging to their feet, one can become of lofty life. Just as the pipal absorbs the palaas tree into itself (and makes it like itself),
Attaching oneself to the Society of the Saints, one is exalted and uplifted, as the palaas tree is absorbed by the peepal tree.
As Butea frondosa plant becomes part and parcel of the Ficus religiosa tree; similarly, meeting with the saints' society, one becomes sublime.
Clinging to the true company one becomes lofty. Just as a pipal growing in a palaas eats up the palaas, so through the true company the palaas of the inner mind was done away with.
9G39: Ram naamai = in Parmatma's Name. Baas = fragrance. ||4||
(in the same way, the person in whom) the fragrance of Parmatma's Name settles becomes of the loftiest life among all beings. ||4||
That mortal being is supreme among all people, who is perfumed by the fragrance of the Lord's Name. ||4||
The mortal, within whom, the fragrance of the Lord's Name abides, becomes the most sublime among men.
O Ram! If the fragrance of Your Name settles in a person's heart, that person becomes the most excellent of all beings. ||4||
QXAA: Nirmal = saving from the dirt of vices, pure. Saakha = branch. Saakha haree = a green branch. Jarreejai = is set, sprouts.

(The person who, through the blessing of the Guru's teaching,) began each day to do the deeds that save from the dirt of vices — (on the tree of their life, as it were, this) green branch keeps sprouting,
One who continually acts in goodness and immaculate purity, sprouts green branches in great abundance.
The body tree, does good many pure and immaculate deeds, ever puts on the green boughs of the Lord's meditation.
Becoming pure, they have done many pure deeds. O Hari! Every day they (jarreejai) plant the (saakha) crop that is Your Names.
3HKG: Gur = the Guru. Drirraia = made firm in the heart. Giaan = understanding of spiritual life. Bahkaar = scent, fragrance. Baas = fragrance. Jag = in the world. Deejai = is given out. ||5||
(which) keeps bearing the flower of dharma, and the fruit of the understanding of spiritual life given by the Guru. The scent and fragrance (of this flower) spreads through (the whole) world. ||5||
The Guru has taught me that Dharmic faith is the flower, and spiritual wisdom is the fruit; this fragrance permeates the world. ||5||
The Guru has instructed me, that faith is the flower and gnosis the fruit is the flower and gnosis the fruit of this tree and bliss the word with scent and fragrance.
For that flower of dharma, the Guru has made firm the fruit of spiritual knowledge; the (bahkaar) spreading fragrance of that flower and fruit — that is, devotion — has been given to the world. ||5||
A2QM: Eko = the One (Parmatma) alone. Man = in the mind. Braham = Parmatma. Drisat = sight, gaze.
(In the whole world) the light of the One (Parmatma alone dwells); the One Parmatma alone dwells in the mind (of all). One should make one's gaze such that it sees only Parmatma in all creation.
The One, the Light of the One, abides within my mind; God, the One, is seen in all.
The One Luminous Lord alone abides within my mind and the Creator-Lord alone is seen among all.
O One Light! You alone are dwelling in my mind. O Braham! I have seen You alone in all.
HTNA: Aatam Ram = Parmatma. Pasre = pervading. Tale = under. ||6||
In all creation the One Parmatma alone is spreading out the expanse; (so) one should place (one's) head beneath the feet of all. ||6||
The One Lord, the Supreme Soul, is spread out everywhere; all place their heads beneath His Feet. ||6||
The One All-pervading soul is spread all over, Everyone places one's head under His feet.
O Ram, the form of the self of all! You alone pervade all places; all place their heads beneath Your feet. ||6||
AC53: Nakte = with noses cut off, disgraced. Tin naak = their nose. Ghas ghas = rubbing again and again. Vadheejai = is cut off.
See: the people who stay without Parmatma's Name bring only disgrace on themselves; their nose is forever being cut off.
Without the Naam, the Name of the Lord, people look like criminals with their noses cut off; bit by bit, their noses are cut off.
The men without the Name look like nose-shorn persons, Gratingly, and gratingly are chopped off their noses.
All who are without Your Name are seen with noses cut off — that is, in this world they are in disrepute, and in the next world too the nose of their good name is rubbed and rubbed and cut off.
SXL8: Saakat = people cut off from Parmatma. Kaheeahi = are called. Dhrig = deserving of reproach. ||7||
People cut off from Parmatma are called egotists alone. A life lived without the Name is only worthy of reproach. ||7||
The faithless cynics are called egotistical; without the Name, their lives are cursed. ||7||
The apostate persons are called the egoists, Without the Name, accursed is their life.
The self-willed who are called egotists — their living is cursed, because they are without Your Name. ||7||
WCG8: Saas = breath. Saas saas = every breath. Jab lag = as long as. Tat = at once. Begal = without hesitation, with faith. Pareejai = one should stay lying.
As long as even one breath is coming in the mind (that is, in the body), one should stay in Parmatma's shelter with full faith.
As long as the breath breathes through the mind deep within, hurry and seek God's Sanctuary.
As long as there is breath and life in your mind, that long, hurriedly and quickly, seek you your Lord's refuge.
So, O Bhagvan! As long as the breath comes and goes in our body, O form of reality (tat), we are (begal) swiftly, with the mind, falling into Your shelter with every breath.
86LR: Nanak (says: O Prabhu!) Show mercy, show mercy (on me), that I may keep washing the feet of Your saints. ||8||4||
Please shower Your Kind Mercy and take pity upon Nanak, that he may wash the feet of the Holy. ||8||4||
O Lord, show You such mercy and Compassion to Nanak, that he may ever wash the feet of Yours saints.
Sri Guru ji says: O mine of grace! Cast such a glance of grace on us that I may keep (pakheejai) beholding the feet of the holy ones. ||8||4||
QVCS: Rama = O Ram! Saadhoo = the Guru. Dhuveejai = may I wash, may I keep washing.
O my Ram! May I keep washing the Guru's feet (every day),
O Lord, I wash the feet of the Holy.
O my All-pervading God, I ever wash the feet of Your saints.
O Ram! May I wash the feet of Your holy ones.
MLVL: Kilbikh = sins. Dahan hohi = are burnt. Thakur = O Thakur! ||1|| Rahau ||
O my Thakur! Show (this) mercy on me. (Staying in the Guru's shelter,) all sins are burnt in an instant. ||1|| Rahau ||
May my sins be burnt away in an instant; O my Lord and Master, please bless me with Your Mercy. ||1||Pause||
My Lord, show You such mercy to me, that my sins be burnt down in an instant. Pause.
O my Thakur ji! Show this grace, by which my sins may be burnt up in an instant. ||1|| Rahau ||
BWHF: Deen = humble. Khare = are standing. Dar = at (Your) door. Thaadhe = standing. At tarsan kau = to those who are longing greatly. Deejai = give.
O Prabhu! Humble beggars are standing at (Your) door; give (this) alms to those who are longing greatly.
The meek and humble beggars stand begging at Your Door. Please be generous and give to those who are yearning.
My Master, the meek alms-men are standing and begging at Your door. Bless You with alms, those exceedingly desirous ones.
We beggars, becoming humble, are standing at Your door; give alms to Your servants who are longing greatly. ☬ If You ask what we are begging for, he says:
JNNF: Traah = save. Prabh = O Prabhu! Mo kau = to me. Drirreejai = make firm in the heart. ||1||
O Prabhu! Save (us from these sins), save (us); (we) have come to (Your) shelter. O Prabhu! Through the Guru's teaching make (Your) Name firm within me. ||1||
Save me, save me, O God - I have come to Your Sanctuary. Please implant the Guru's Teachings, and the Naam within me. ||1||
Save me and redeem, me, O Lord, I have sought Your protection, Implant You within me, the Guru's instruction and Yours Name.
O Prabhu! Protect us, protect us; we have come to Your shelter. Give me the Guru's teaching and make the Name certain in me. ||1||
96DC: Nagar mah = in the city of the body. Sabla = (sa-bal) mighty. Uth = rising. Joojh = battle. Kareejai = I do.
O Prabhu! In the city (of the body of us beings), lust, anger (and every other vice) stays mighty; one has to rise up again and again, always, and do battle (with them).
Sexual desire and anger are very powerful in the body-village; I rise up to fight the battle against them.
Very-powerful are lust and wrath in the body township. Getting ready ever wage I war with them.
In the city of the body, lust and anger have grown very strong; every day one must rise up again and again and (joojh) fight them.
MS13: Angeekaar = siding with, help, support. Raakh levahu = save. Kaadh kadheejai = take out for ever. ||2||
O Prabhu! Help (us); save (us from these). (Uniting us with) the perfect Guru, take (us) out (of their clutches). ||2||
Please make me Your Own and save me; through the Perfect Guru, I drive them out. ||2||
Making me Your own, save You me, O Lord, that, by the grace of the perfect Guru, I may drive them out.
So, O Maharaj, save me from the enemies lust and the rest, and take my side; uniting me with the perfect Guru, (kaadh) pull me out of this mire. ||2||
REP0: Sabal at = very mighty. Bikhia agan = the fire of (craving for) Maya. Hiv = snow, ice. Sabad gur = the Guru's Word.
Within (beings) the fire of (craving for) Maya is blazing fiercely. Give the Guru's Word, cool as ice, (so that) great peace may arise in body and mind.
The powerful fire of corruption is raging violently within; the Word of the Guru's Shabad is the ice water which cools and soothes.
Within me is greatly raging the war of sins. O my Lord, bless You me with the icy-cold Guru's word, that it may be quenched.
Within the heart the fire of the sense-objects is burning exceedingly strong; to put it out, give us the Guru's Word, cool as (hiv) ice.

9EFG: Tan = in the body. Man = in the mind. Adhikaaee = much. Sookh = in peace. Saveejai = can be enjoyed, absorption may come. ||3||
(The Guru's Word) cuts away every disease (of beings); (through the blessing of the Guru's Word) one can stay immersed in spiritual bliss. ||3||
My mind and body are calm and tranquil; the disease has been cured, and now I sleep in peace. ||3||
My body and mind are absolutely tranquillised and being rid of my malady, I now sleep in peace.
Then may great peace come into our body and mind, may the disease of birth and the rest be cut away, and may we sleep in peace. ||3||
N8D2: Ravia = is pervading. Sarab thaaee = in all places. Ghat ghat = in every body. Raveejai = is pervading.
Just as the sun, through (its) rays, reaches all places, (so) Parmatma pervades every body in all creation.
As the rays of the sun spread out everywhere, the Lord pervades each and every heart.
As the sun's rays pervade all the places, so is the Lord contained in all the hearts.
Just as the sun by its rays pervades all places, so, O all-pervading One, You pervade all places.
1K4B: Ras = bliss, taste. Paavai = enjoys. Tat = essence. Nij = one's own. Ghar = in the home. Nij ghar = in one's own true home, at Prabhu's feet. ||4||
The person who meets the saints enjoys the taste (of union). (Through the company of the saints,) absorbed at Prabhu's feet, the taste of the Name can be drunk. ||4||
Meeting the Holy Saint, one drinks in the Sublime Essence of the Lord; sitting in the home of your own inner being, drink in the essence. ||4||
If man meets with the Guru, the saint of the saints, he attains the Name-Nectar and in drinks the quintessence, even while sitting in his own home.
When the most excellent holy ones are met, then the soul gains the taste of Your Name, and, established in its own body, keeps drinking that (tat) essence of taste. ||4||
XXVA: Kau = to. Setee = with. Dekh = seeing, waiting for. Sooreejai = the sun.
The devotee (of Parmatma) keeps (such) love for the Guru as the chakvi (passes the night of separation) waiting and waiting for (the rising of) the sun.
The humble being is in love with the Guru, like the chakvi bird which loves to see the sun.
God's slave so loves the Guru, as the she-ruddy goose loves to see the sun.
The Gurmukhs have love for the Guru, just as the chakvi looks for the sun.
LM3E: Nirkhat = while watching. Rain sabh = the whole night. Nirkhee = watches, keeps waiting. Mukh kaadhai = (when the sun) shows its face. Amrit = the water of the Name that gives spiritual life. ||5||

Watching and watching, (the chakvi) keeps watching the whole night through; (when the sun) shows its face (then she gains union with the chakva. In the same way, when the Guru gives His sight, the servant) can drink the water of the Name that gives spiritual life. ||5||
She watches, and keeps on watching all through the night; and when the sun shows its face, she drinks in the Amrit. ||5||
She watches, and keeps on watching all the night through and in-drinks Nectar when the sun shows his face.

In the same way, the whole night of life was passed (nirkhat nirkhat) waiting and waiting for the sun that is the Guru. When the Guru-sun showed its face (rose), then I drank the nectar of attaining You. ||5||
87DL: Saakat = people cut off from Parmatma. Suan = dogs. Kaheeahi = are called. Durmat = evil intellect.
People cut off from Parmatma are very greedy; they are called dogs (in nature); (within them) the dirt of evil intellect stays (always) filled.
The faithless cynic is said to be very greedy - he is a dog. He is overflowing with the filth and pollution of evil-mindedness.
The cur like mammon-worshipper is said to be very avaricious. He is filled with an excessive filth of evil-thoughts.
Again, those called (saakat) self-willed are very greedy, like dogs; their inner mind is filled with the dirt of evil intellect.
JW88: Suai = for (their own) purpose. Karahi = do (plural). Visaah = trust. Kia keejai = what can be done? It cannot be done. ||6||
(Saakat people) say many things for their own purpose, but they should not be trusted. ||6||
He talks excessively about his own interests. How can he be trusted? ||6||
For his own self-interest, he talks much. What reliance can be placed on him?
The self-willed say many things for their own ends; so what trust is to be placed in those selfish ones? ||6||
N04F: O Hari! Give (me) the company of (Your) saints and devotees. Meeting in the company of the saints, the taste of Parmatma's Name can be gained.
I have sought the Sanctuary of the Saadh Sangat, the Company of the Holy; I have found the Sublime Essence of the Lord.
I have sought the refuge of the society of the saints, and the devotees, through which I have found the Lord's elixir.
I have found the shelter of the company of the (saadh) most excellent holy ones, in which, O Hari, the (kaadh) treasure that is the taste of Your Name has (kadheejai) come forth.
CQS7: Par upkaar = the good of others. Bolahi mukh = speak with the mouth. Har = O Hari! Deejai = give. Sant bhagat = the company of saints and devotees. ||7||
The saints keep speaking words for the good of others with (their) mouth; the saints are of countless virtues. Grant (me the company) of (those) saints and devotees. ||7||
They do good deeds for others, and speak of the Lord's many Glorious Virtues; please bless me to meet these Saints, these devotees of the Lord. ||7||
My Lord, bless You me, with the society of the supreme saints and devotees, who narrate Yours myriad virtues and do good to others.
O Hari! Your devotees of many virtues, the foremost, the form of peace and full of virtue, speak of virtues for the good of others; place Your servant in their company. ||7||
0GUT: Daia pat = master of mercy, merciful. Daata = giver of gifts. Sabh = all creation.
O Prabhu! You are unreachable, the source of mercy, the Master of mercy, the giver of gifts to all beings. Show mercy and protect all beings.
You are the Inaccessible Lord, Kind and Compassionate, the Great Giver; please shower us with Your Mercy, and save us.
O my Unfathomable, Compassionate and Beneficent Lord of grace, showering Yours benediction save You us all.
O Merciful One! You are unreachable, the Lord of mercy and the Giver; in mercy, protect all.
VTYM: Jeea = (plural of the word jeeu) beings. Jag jeevan = Prabhu, the life of the world. Kareejai = do. ||8||5||
Nanak says: (O Prabhu!) All beings are Yours; You alone are the support of the whole world. Sustain (all). ||8||5||
You are the Life of all the beings of the world; please cherish and sustain Nanak. ||8||5||
O Lord, You alone are the vital-breath of all the beings and the world. Sustain You me, Your slave Nanak.

You alone are the one life-breath of the beings of the whole world. Sri Guru ji says: You Yourself are the sustainer of all — meaning, sustain us. ||8||5|| ☬ Speaking of the glory of the dust of the saints' feet, he describes the manner of praying:
W5DK: Rama = O Ram! Ham = us (beings). Kareejai = keep (us so).
O Ram! Keep us the servants of (Your) servants.
O Lord, please make me the slave of Your slaves.
O my all-pervading God, make You me, the slave of Yours slaves.
O Ram! Make us the servants of Your servants.
TY3Q: Jab lag = as long as. Saas = breath. Saadhoo dhoor = the dust of the saints' feet. Piveejai = should be drunk. ||1|| Rahau ||

As long as breath is coming in the body, one should keep drinking the dust of the saints' feet (staying humbly in the saints' company, one should keep drinking the nectar of the Name from them). ||1|| Rahau ||
As long as there is breath deep within my mind, let me drink in the dust of the Holy. ||1||Pause||
As long as there is breath in my mind, You make me eat the dust of the feet of the saints. Pause.
As long as there is breath in our body, let us, turning the mind inward, drink the dust of the holy ones' feet. ||1|| Rahau ||
S33B: Sankar = Shiv. Sekhnaag = Sheshnaag. Locheejai = is longed for.
Shiv, Narad, Sheshnaag (and every rishi and) muni have longed for the dust of the saints' feet.
Shiva, Naarad, the thousand-headed cobra king and the silent sages long for the dust of the Holy.
Shiva, Narad, Cobra King and the silent sages long for the dust of saints' feet.
For Shiv, Narad ji, Sheshnaag and the great munis — all of these want the dust of the saints' feet.
PM2H: Hohi = become (plural). Sabh = all. Jah = where. ||1||
Wherever the saints set their feet, all those realms, all those places, become pure. ||1||
All the worlds and realms where the Holy place their feet are sanctified. ||1||
Every house and abode, where the saints place their feet becomes sanctified.
The (bhavan) house where Your saints set their feet, (bhavan) wandering on the pretext of seeking alms and the like — (all those realms become pure). ||1||
G3KL: Taj = giving up. Sabh = all. Tajeeai = should be given up. Sang = in the company. Mil = joining.
Giving up concern for what people think, one should give up all pride (in any greatness of one's own), and stay joined in the company of the saints.
So let go of your shame and renounce all your egotism; join with the Saadh Sangat, the Company of the Holy, and remain there.
Shed you your shame, renounce all ego and meet and live with the saints.
Giving up shame, let us give up all ego too, and keep the mind always joined in the company of the holy ones.
N5Z7: Kaan = dependence, dread. Chukavai = ends. Bikh = in the poisonous world-ocean that brings spiritual death. ||2||
(The person who stays in the company of the saints) ends the dread of Dharamraj. (The saints) pull out the one drowning in the poisonous world-ocean that brings spiritual death. ||2||
Give up your fear of the Righteous Judge of Dharma, and you shall be lifted up and saved from drowning in the sea of poison. ||2||
The will make you shed the fear of the Righteous judge and extricate you form drowning in the sea of poison.
Let my mind be freed from the dread of Dharamrai, and pull it out from the (kaadh) things that are poison. ||2||
73S0: Bharam = because of wandering. Sooke = of dried-up spiritual life. Ubh suk = trees dried up where they stand. Kaheeahi = are called. Hareejai = become green.

(The people who,) falling into the wandering (of Maya), lose the freshness of spiritual life are called like trees that dry up where they stand; (but even such people of dried-up life,) joining the company of the saints, become green.
Some are standing, parched and shrivelled up by their doubts; joining the Saadh Sangat, they are rejuvenated.
They, who are parched by doubt are thoroughly dried up while standing. Meeting with the society of saints they blossom forth again.

Those in whose inner mind much doubt has spread are called (ubh suk) dried up where they stand — meaning without virtue; they too, joining the company of the holy, (hareejai) become green — meaning they become full of virtues.
A7YK: Ta te = therefore. Bilam = (vilamb) delay. Na keejai = should not be made. Jai = going. ||3||
Therefore not even a moment's delay should be made. One should go (quickly) and cling to the feet of the saints. ||3||
So do not delay, even for an instant - go and fall at the feet of the Holy. ||3||
Therefore make you not even a moment's delay and go and fall you at the feet of the saints.
So, O Bhagvan, show this grace: that, growing slack, there may not be even a moment's (bilam) delay; let us go and cling to the feet of Your holy ones. ||3||
CFSL: Ratan vath = precious thing. Rakheejai = is kept.
Parmatma's Name, Parmatma's praise, is a precious thing. Parmatma has kept this thing with the saints.
The Kirtan of the Praise of the Lord's Name is a priceless jewel. The Lord has given it for the Holy to keep.
The praise of the Lord's Name is an invaluable treasure, which God has deposited with the saint.
O Ram! Your kirtan and Your jewel-like Name — O Hari, You have kept these with Your holy ones.
B8KH: Bachan gur = the Guru's word. Sat kar = with faith. Maane = accepts (singular). Dhareejai = is placed, places. ||4||
The person who accepts the Guru's teaching with full faith — (the Guru) takes out (this precious thing) and places it before them. ||4||
Whoever accepts and follows the Word of the Guru's Teachings as True - this Jewel is taken out and given to him. ||4||
Whosoever accepts the Guru's word as true abiding, taking out this treasure, the Guru places it before him.
The person who accepts the Guru's words as true, true — before that person the saints take out the thing that is the Name and set it down. O Hari, let us give this very teaching. ||4||
6YDT: Jan = O people! Bhaee = O brothers! Gur = the Guru. Kaadhee = has raised. Kukeejai = is calling out.
O saints! O brothers! The Guru has raised (His) arm and is calling out: listen (to His words) with attention.
Listen, O Saints; listen, humble Siblings of Destiny: the Guru raises His Arms and sends out the call.
Hear and attend to, you, brother, saintly persons, the Guru raises his arm and calls to them.
O brothers! O saints! Listen with mind and speech: the Guru raises His arm high and calls out.
5GME: Aatam kau = for the soul. Sukh sukh = peace at every moment. Paveejai = one should fall. ||5||
O saints! If you want lasting peace for your soul, then you should stay in the Guru's shelter. ||5||
If you long for everlasting peace and comfort for your soul, then enter the Sanctuary of the True Guru. ||5||
If you desire everlasting bliss, and happiness for your soul, then enter you the sanctuary of the True Guru.
So, O brothers! If you want nothing but peace for your soul every day, then fall into the True Guru's shelter. ||5||
RTEQ: Vad bhaag = great fortune. Neeka = beautiful. Drirreejai = should be made firm in the heart.
If a person's fortune is great and good, then, taking the Guru's teaching, they make Parmatma's Name firm (within themselves).
If you have great good fortune and are very noble, then implant the Guru's Teachings and the Naam, the Name of the Lord, within.
If you are blessed with great good fortune and are very virtuous, then implant the Lord's Name within you through the Guru's instructions.
If one's fortune is exceedingly great, then, taking the Guru's teaching, let us make the Name firm. ☬ Now he tells its fruit:
DC60: Bikham = difficult. Tareeai = can be crossed. Sahje = in spiritual poise. Peejai = can be drunk. ||6||

Attachment to Maya — all this is a very difficult world-ocean; (through the blessing of the Name it) can be crossed. (So,) staying in spiritual poise, one should drink the taste of Parmatma's Name. ||6||
Emotional attachment to Maya is totally treacherous; drinking in the Sublime Essence of the Lord, you shall easily, intuitively cross over the world-ocean. ||6||
The love is riches is all too troublesome, in-drinking the Lord's Name-elixir crosses the world-ocean.
By drinking Hari's taste, all the attachment to Maya that is so hard in the world is crossed with ease. ||6||
V8XY: Adhikaaee = great (lovers). Pachai pacheejai = burns at every moment.
The people who are great lovers of Maya alone (always suffer. The lover of Maya) keeps burning at every moment in (the fire of craving for) Maya.
Those who are totally in love with Maya, Maya, shall rot away in Maya.
They, who are the great lovers of mammon or Maya, in mammon they putrefy.
Those whose love is for Maya and Maya alone are rotting in Maya and make others rot.
ZNFV: Agiaan = ignorance of spiritual life. Andher = darkness. Panth = the road (of life). Bikhrra = difficult. Ahankaar = with ego. Bhaar = with the load. Ahankaar bhaar = with the load of ego. Lad leejai = is loaded. ||7||
(For such a person) ignorance of spiritual life (becomes) pitch darkness; the road (of life) becomes hard (for them), (because they) stay (always) loaded with the load of ego. ||7||
The path of ignorance and darkness is utterly treacherous; they are loaded down with the crushing load of egotism. ||7||
Exceedingly gloomy and arduous is the path of spiritual ignorance and the mortal is loaded with the heavy load of self-conceit.
In their inner mind is the great darkness of ignorance, and ahead the road of Yama is hard, on which they must walk; and through ego they have loaded on the burden of sin. ||7||
VLW9: Ram = all-pervading. Ramu = remember. Ramai te = from Parmatma (His Name) alone. Gat = lofty spiritual state. Keejai = is made, is attained.
O Nanak! Keep remembering the Name of the all-pervading Ram. From the Name of the all-pervading Ram alone can the lofty spiritual state be gained.
O Nanak, chanting the Name of the Lord, the All-pervading Lord, one is emancipated.
Nanak, the Beauteous Lord is pervading all over, Uttering, and reciting the Lord's Name, one is emancipated.
Sri Guru ji says: chanting and chanting (ram ram) Ram, who is (ram) beautifully all-pervading, let us attain our liberation from (Ramai) Parmeshar.
C4VS: Drirrae = makes firm in the heart. Naamai = in the Name itself. Ralai = merges. Mileejai = one becomes united. Chhaka = a collection of six hymns. ||8||6|| Chhaka 1 ||

When the Guru is met, He makes (Parmatma's) Name firm (in a person's heart). (The person) merges for ever in Parmatma's Name. Chhaka = a set of six, a collection of six (ashtapadis). ||8||6|| Chhaka 1 ||
Meeting the True Guru, the Naam is implanted within; we are united and blended with the Lord's Name. ||8||6|| First Set of Six||
If the True Guru meets, then, enshrines he, the Name within the man's and he unites within the man's mind and he unites and meets with the Lord's Name.
But if the True Guru is met, He makes the Name firm; then one merges and mingles in Ram's Name. ||8||6||
